summary: Postinstall and import-time beacon exfiltrates host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package declares a postinstall script that runs beacon.cjs, which POSTs a JSON payload containing the installer's hostname, install path, current working directory, package name, and Node.js version to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc over plaintext HTTP. The main entry (index.js) also invokes beacon.fire() at require time, so the same exfiltration occurs whenever a consumer imports the module. The rest of the package is a stub: index.js exports a Proxy of no-op functions and provides no real functionality consistent with the @ppa-web-components scope name. The combination of a scoped name resembling an internal component namespace, absence of real functionality, hardcoded non-publisher bare-IP destination, plaintext HTTP, and automatic firing at both install and import time collects reconnaissance data useful for follow-on dependency-confusion attacks against the installer environment.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
